answer: Neighborhood Ridge Scoring. Each agent's messages propagate only across edges whose endpoints share a verified interaction history; the score is the median path length to distinct clusters. New nodes must sit near a ridge of accumulated umber activity before their traffic is relayed. Sybils multiply but stay isolated, paying repeated relay latency and lost reach per fake node. A violet tag marks clusters that absorb too many fresh leaves and caps their outbound fanout, so attackers must buy real history for each identity.
